title: A burst, then the refill
request:
ten tokens a second with a burst of five, spent at 0 ms, 100 ms and much later

./your_program.sh token-bucket
init 10 5
take 0 5
take 0 1
take 100 1
take 100 1
take 100000 5
note: 100 ms at ten a second is exactly one token, and the take at 100 000 ms finds five rather than a thousand: the cap is what makes a bucket a bucket. Note that the two takes at 100 ms answer differently — the clock has not moved, so nothing has been added between them.

title: A queue that drains rather than fills
request:
a queue of three draining at ten a second, offered work at 0 ms and 200 ms

./your_program.sh leaky-bucket
init 10 3
offer 0 3
offer 0 1
offer 200 2
offer 200 2
note: The leaky bucket refuses rather than delays: there is no queue of pending answers here, only a level that says whether the next unit fits. Accepting work and reporting a queue longer than the capacity is the mistake to watch for.
